_doc: Phase-1 source allowlist. See specs/content-in-db.md §3.3. Adding a source is a reviewed commit, never a silent change. Directory sites (Toolify, TAAFT, Futurepedia) are deliberately absent: their ordering is SimilarWeb traffic — so aggregating several of them counts one signal repeatedly while looking like corroboration — and their top placements are purchasable.
_placementDoc: Reviewed listings hold `leading`, ordered by the fused score. Anything the job discovers goes to `emerging` and only when at least minCorroborationForNew sources rank it. Phase-1 sources cannot carry `leading` on their own: with GitHub the only true ranking source for repos, an unguarded run put three unknown keyword matches above aider, cline and continue.

sources.label: StartupBase
sources.note: Single bulk llms-full.txt published by the site for machine use; ai.txt permits discovery and classification. Every record carries a paragraph description and a launch date.

sources.label: GitHub (agent-skills topics)
sources.note: topic:agent-skills / topic:claude-skills. The generic repo search found 2-3 skills per category and none in two of them, which read as a thin ecosystem; the topics carry 12,313 and 6,084 repos respectively, so the search was wrong, not the world. A topic is the author's own classification, so precision is high enough to place a listing without a second origin — which is required, since every skill source is GitHub and could never reach two.

sources.label: Hacker News
sources.note: Corroboration only. A bare domain on HN means someone posted a link, not that the thing is a product — ranking raw domains put arstechnica.com above every real coding agent. Domains score only when they already match a listing; discovery is limited to GitHub links, where the URL proves what it is.

sources.label: Product Hunt
sources.note: Free non-expiring developer token from producthunt.com/v2/oauth/applications. Queried by topic slug (see phTopics) — an earlier version passed query.split(' ')[0], which is 'ai' for every category and is not a valid slug, so this source silently returned zero rows for all 25 categories while reporting no error. selfPlacing because a PH post is an explicit product submission with votes, not a text match; and because PH is the only saas discovery source, so the two-origin rule would otherwise keep saas/emerging permanently empty.

sources.label: npm downloads (last year)
sources.note: Only contributes for listings that already carry package_name. The seed corpus has none, so this source is inert until package names are filled in — it is wired up rather than pretended away.

sources.label: Zapier app directory
sources.note: Undocumented public JSON. Category-shaped taxonomy with an AI sub-tree; carries description + vendor domain. robots.txt disallows /api/, so harvest politely and never put it on a request path.

_queryDoc: Search terms per category. Absent categories fall back to the category name. Keep these narrow: a broad term returns the whole field and drowns the specific tools.
_mergedFrom: resources/content/wt-sources.json (5 categories); its github_keywords are folded into queries below. That file and .agents/skills/wt-ingest are retired — the refresh job owns discovery now.
_selfPlacingDoc: A source may place a discovered listing alone when its match is an explicit classification (a topic) rather than a text match. minCorroborationForNew still governs everything else.
_skillQueryDoc: Short terms for the topic-scoped skill search. GitHub ANDs every term with the topic filter, so a full category query returns nothing: 'topic:agent-skills ai pdf document processing' is 0 results while 'topic:agent-skills pdf' is 141. One or two words only.
_classifyDoc: Keyword rules for placing a swept skill repo into a category. Order matters: the first match wins, so specific rules come before generic ones. 'agent'/'agentic' deliberately does NOT map to workflow-automation — almost every agent skill mentions agents, so that rule swallowed everything, including mattpocock/skills ('Skills for Real Engineers').
_phTopicDoc: Product Hunt topic slugs, verified against the topics API. The job previously passed query.split(' ')[0], which is 'ai' for every category — and 'ai' is not a slug, so Product Hunt returned zero rows for all 25 categories while reporting no error. PH's taxonomy is much coarser than ours, so several categories share a topic; that is the real shape of the source, not a gap.

excludedTools._doc: Rows the discovery must never place again, whatever a source says. Keyed by tool_slug. This is a safety list, not a taste list — a row belongs here when listing it would put a reader at risk, not when it is merely off-topic (that is what the assignment gate is for).
excludedTools.abwor9658-social-media-skills: README is a Download-for-Windows page for a ZIP committed in the repo, with instructions to run the .exe and click through SmartScreen. Found 2026-08-03 during per-row verification.
excludedTools.aditya923-c-xpoz-agent-skills: Same shape, same instructions; also an unattributed copy of XPOZpublic/xpoz-agent-skills, so it duplicated a row already listed.
